KEY DETAILS DATE & TIME Early morning hours of Sunday, November 15, 2026 (exact time not released) LOCATION State Route 215 at Nolan Road, Okanogan, WA VICTIM One pedestrian struck and killed; identity not released ROAD CLOSURES SR 215 was shut down while police investigated INVESTIGATION Okanogan County Sheriff’s Office investigating with WSP, Omak PD and Colville Tribal Police; driver and vehicle not yet located; tips: (509) 422-7200 A pedestrian died after being struck by a vehicle at State Route 215 and Nolan Road near Okanogan in the early morning hours of Sunday, November 15, 2026. Okanogan County deputies responded to reports of a traffic collision and found one person dead at the scene. Witnesses told deputies the driver allegedly kept going without stopping. Investigators are still working to locate the driver and the vehicle, and authorities have not released the victim’s identity.
 According to NewsRadio 560 KPQ, the Okanogan County Sheriff’s Office is leading the investigation with help from the Washington State Patrol, the Omak Police Department and the Colville Tribal Police Department. KHQ reported that SR 215 was shut down while police investigated, and that the Sheriff’s Office said the circumstances of the collision remain under investigation. Officials have not released any details about the vehicle or driver. Anyone who saw the crash or has information about the driver is asked to call the Okanogan County Sheriff’s Office at (509) 422-7200.

 RCW 46.52.020 – DUTY IN CASE OF INJURY OR DEATH OFFICIAL TEXT ↗ Under RCW 46.52.020, a driver involved in a collision that injures or kills a person must immediately stop at or as close as possible to the scene, remain there, give their name, address, insurance and vehicle information, and render reasonable assistance to anyone injured. A driver who fails to do so in a crash that results in death commits a class B felony. A hit-and-run driver’s failure to stop can also be important evidence in a civil claim.
 RCW 4.20.010 – WRONGFUL DEATH OFFICIAL TEXT ↗ RCW 4.20.010 allows a wrongful death lawsuit when a person’s death is caused by the wrongful act, neglect or default of another. The claim is brought by the personal representative of the deceased person’s estate on behalf of eligible family members. When a hit-and-run driver has not been identified, families may also be able to look to uninsured motorist coverage.
 This summary is general information, not legal advice. Every case depends on its specific facts.
